verdict.tagline: A brilliant reimagining of a classic, though technical turbulence remains.
for_you_if: you want a modern retelling of a classic sci-fi shooter

you expect modern controller support out of the box

claims.claim: Reviewers experience frequent crashes during gameplay, loading screens, or specific chapters.

citations.review_text:
Good game. A great update and expansion on the original. I would reccomend.

There were some audio glitches, like sfx cutting out, voices being very quiet, and although there are some great musical moments, if you die it just cuts out and doesn't come back when you respawn, which is dissapointing.

Loading times are pretty bad.

I started on the steam deck, but it got very difficult to switch weapons, the steam input integration didn't seem great, and in some outdoor sections the pefromance tanked. So I ended up playing it on my PC with keyboard and mouse, which was much easier.

Partway through playing, I opted into the beta build, which greatly improved the menuing experience, which was not good, though I haven't tried it on the deck again yet, maybe it's fixed some things.

A must play title if there ever was one.  You can really feel the love that the dev team put into this.  

It's also in the process of getting a major update as well.  I tried the new beta and was impressed with the new improvements.  Strangely, said beta ran smooth as silk during regular gameplay but every instance of loading would cause a hard crash. Eventually got frustrated and did a rollback to an earlier version to finish the game, 

This goes on sale for cheap often.  Half-Life fan or not, this is a game not to be missed.

this game is very much worth it, even now. I loved the start, and the finally fight was cool. tho I will be honest, their are parts that needs to be pointed out. Zen feels way too long. I loved the first chapter, but it does outstay it's welcome by the end and you just wished that was it.

For Windows Users: Black Mesa is an incredible passion project that was lucky enough to catch the attention of Valve to be their semi-official HL1 remake.
I absolutely loved this game, the combat is smooth, seems to be similar enough to the original with easy mod support and a fairly decent community; I loved playing this game, the ending levels drag but tmk HL1 drags in general so it's not so much a complaint for this game. I love moving through the world, no yellow paint, it's "video game-y" in the perfect mix- just enough to immerse you while keeping a fun pace.

It's unfortunately very difficult to play and recommend on Linux, which is why I have to not recommend:
-Constant crashes due to memory leaks (from new UI + proton) / doesn't work without proton
-Texture issues I couldn't fix where the entire game would turn pink / warped
-Audio Settings do not change when changing the slide bars
-Player character will warp randomly and block sight while holding some weapons (I had multiple instances swapping to my shotgun I'd see my body spasm in front of the POV, blocking lines of sight, this also happened with that charge energy gun too.)

I cannot under emphasize the crashes on linux, luckily I basically spam F6 to quick save but I crashes almost every 10 minutes due to the memory leaks and there's absolutely nothing you can do about it... Proton DB has some slight fixes but you will keep crashing over and over and over... I will flip my rating when the game becomes more optimized and stable for Linux; but unfortunately I can't recommend a game that doesn't want to run.

Looks great. Runs buttery smooth on High at 60 fps. No notable bugs from anything during single-player.

///--HOWEVER--\\\

It crashes almost as much as Fallout 76. Even on medium and lowest settings.
For seemingly no reason whatsoever. IDK why, at least not for certain.
But if I had to guess it's a memory leak due to quick-save/loading.
It has also given me some of the most terrifying crashes I've ever seen.
Such as a full BSOD and a weird one that made the screen look like a 75% - 25% pie chart with my default windows color and a black triangle.
It crashes so often it even triggered an automatic bug report for my hardware.
NOT A HARDWARE PROBLEM. NOT A SETTINGS PROBLEM. NOT A POWERSAVING PROBLEM.
100% in game problem. Reproducible.

///DO NOT BUY UNLESS YOU HAVE A HIGH TOLERANCE FOR CRASHES\\\

Better off buying the original if you want the full HL experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that controller support and steam input integration feel clunky, particularly when trying to switch weapons.

citations.review_text:
Good game. A great update and expansion on the original. I would reccomend.

There were some audio glitches, like sfx cutting out, voices being very quiet, and although there are some great musical moments, if you die it just cuts out and doesn't come back when you respawn, which is dissapointing.

Loading times are pretty bad.

I started on the steam deck, but it got very difficult to switch weapons, the steam input integration didn't seem great, and in some outdoor sections the pefromance tanked. So I ended up playing it on my PC with keyboard and mouse, which was much easier.

Partway through playing, I opted into the beta build, which greatly improved the menuing experience, which was not good, though I haven't tried it on the deck again yet, maybe it's fixed some things.

I played the original for about 7 hours and decided to switch to this at some point just to see the differences and maybe see if this is a better experience. It is not. I was looking for controller support, as I have arthritis and the controller is easier on my hands. The controls for controller are pretty bad and there is no aim assist. Specifically switching weapons is horrendous, which is 90% of the gameplay. Visuals wise the game looks "better" than the original but the visual clarity has become way worse. You can't pick out enemies from the background and everything is a tad bit too dark; the flashlight doesn't light it up enough to compensate. The elegant design that was a necessity in the original because of the limitations has not been replicated here. The soundtrack is PHENOMENAL but I won't get to hear it in-game if I can't even make it to the parts that it plays in! I do not recommend playing this over the original, I genuinely think this is one step forward two steps back.

claims.claim: Reviewers find first-person platforming sections difficult and clunky due to level geometry and traversal design.

citations.review_text: I wish there was middle-ground. On one hand, you can marvel on the amount of work and dedication went into the game. And once you see Xen, it becomes apparent why it took so long to complete those levels. But on the other hand - this is much clunkier than the original GoldSRC or Source port of the original Half-life. You'll constantly bump level geometry and traversal frequently sucks. But the reason I'm leaving this comment  is to tell whoever designed the Gonarch lair and Factory levels and gameplay can eat a bag of dicks. Worst game design with player traversal I ever saw. And, despite visually the Xen levels are impossibly beautiful, I'm glad that the original Half-Life had Xen chapter short.

Faithful remake. They added a ton of stuff to Xen, which is the only major departure from the original. It's pretty ambitious lol. Unfortunately, it felt like I was playing a Source Mod at some moments in Xen. Majority of it is well-polished, though. Had a few rage moments clipping the environment with the jump pack while in chase sequences, but other than that, had a great time. Well done.

lackluster remake of the original. Graphics are a nice upgrade over the original but nothing crazy for the time it was released. They kept a lot of the charm from the original which I really appreciate.

The combat just doesnt really do it for me half the time, damage from the shotgun and explosive weapons feel very inconsistent. Really takes the fun and flow out of the combat if the same enemy sometimes takes 2 double barrel shots to kill and other times only one single barrel shot. Grenade physics are janky which was fine in the original but should have been something they fixed.

Enemy encounters are a big mixed bag as well, the alien encounters are fine, especially when the guns behave. soldier encounters are a pain in the ass. sometimes feels like they take way too many shots to kill and they love spamming grenades the second you leave their line of sight. the assassins are massive pushovers which is the complete reverse experience I had with the original.

The random platform sections were the last nail in the coffin for me, janky controls, inconsistent auto crouch jump made me finally stop bullying myself and play something else.

5/10 missed oppertunity, play the original (not the source port) if you want to experience this game

claims.claim: The Xen chapters are described as significantly extended and feeling repetitive or tedious due to repeated puzzles and sequences.

citations.review_text:
Game is a very good recreation of black mesa (Half-life 1). Quite enjoyed playing it. However, the Xen chapters quite tiring and frustrating due to repetion. by repetion, I mean to move to next area player requires to open the gate and player has to do same thing three or more times. espeacially, in last part, to climb to the top of the tower you have to do the same thing over and over again. It felt like developers use the same thing too much to make the Xen part longer although the Xen part was good enough without unneedless repetion.

Note: Just play the damn game it's the Half-life for God's sake 😁😁😁

The game matches or exceeds the quality of the original Half-Life — for the most part. A notable exception is the Interloper chapter, which is frustratingly convoluted. It's basically a puzzle stacked on another puzzle in a seemingly endless loop, with disproportionately little sense of accomplishment to compensate for the immense amount of frustration. Thankfully the final chapter redeems itself by being much better than the original. Overall, a great remake, although I personally recommend skipping the Interloper chapter if you have played the original for a more cohesive experience.

It is more than an overhaul and a remaster. It is a remake of the old Half Life. It feels classic, it plays modern. Really really good.

Edit: I just finished the game. It is really good. I would give it a solid 8/10. The only reason why it loses some points is the last levels, especially Interloper. So unnecessarily long, complicated and convoluted. Remove that level and the game would have been a 9 or even 10. But it is good nonetheless.

I'm only giving it a negative review because I expected it to be more or less a straightforward remake, just with better graphics. However, this is more like Half-Life With Better Graphics And Extra Content... and, having just replayed the original Half-Life, almost all the added stuff in this game just felt like unnecessary padding.

Obviously, this is subjective, and just because I found that "more is less" here, doesn't mean that you would too.

To me, Black Mesa only had a single addition that made sense: the vortigaunt village, because it showed their role more clearly than the original game did.

But all the other added stuff... it wasn't actively bad, but I just found I didn't care about any of it. For example, there were a bunch of extra enemy spawns, which just forced you to spend more time in the same area rather than moving on. Or the entire Xen section got extended so much that it felt like it got at least 10 times longer. The alien factory had those power connector puzzles that just felt bland (and endless). The Gonarch section became so long that it could've been its own game, seriously.

And then I replayed the original game, which never overstayed its welcome - and I wondered what the point of a remake even was.
